newsitem.title: USA: Group to file FEC complaint against Ralph Nader.
newsitem.headline: Group to file FEC complaint against Ralph Nader.

text.p: A California consumer group said it will file a complaint Monday with the Federal Election Commission against Ralph Nader for failing to register as a presidential candidate and disclose his personal and campaign finances.

Nader, a well-known consumer advocate, has repeatedly said that he does not intend to file any disclosure reports with the FEC and that he is not legally required to do so since he will spend less than $5,000 on his campaign.
But the group filing the complaint, Nader Watch: A Project of Voter Revolt, said Nader had held press conferences, given interviews and discussed his campaign in at least 12 cities.

"Mr. Nader's campaign travel expenditures alone appear to exceed $5,000," the group said in its complaint. "In addition, even greater expenditures appear to have been made on behalf of Mr. Nader's campaign, and with his cooperation, by the Green Party."

The Green Party's nominating convention and a four-day conference held in conjunction with the convention were reported by the San Francisco Chronicle to have cost approximately $25,000, the complaint continued.

"We urge you to take whatever action is necessary to bring Mr. Nader into compliance with the law and provide members of the public the financial information they are entitled to regarding this candidate," the group said.
